Every item handmade by a Haitian has to tell a story of hardship, a businessman named Thomas tells Gigi, who is hoping he will connect his international customers to the luxury goods she sells at her boutique in Haiti. “The client wants a personal connection with a poor Haitian woman in the slums,” Thomas explains.
Morisseau cements herself as a playwright as incisive and curious as she is incredibly entertaining.

Morisseau (Skeleton Crew, Pipeline, Confederates) offers an affecting, engaging, often funny yet fundamentally human (and messy) exploration of relationships, otherness, colonialism, class and identity.

cn.t: Morisseau's thoughtful, perceptive exploration of Haitian identity and family earns strong praise from critics. The play deftly examines cultural tensions between estranged cousins while offering a witty, nuanced portrait that honors its roots.
